OS Command Injection in Background Thread (Falcon) — Remote code execution via background thread shell execution [verified: Same thread_function command injection as finding [1]; the line reference 63 is the cmd construction line immediately before os.system at line 64. User-controlled GET parameter reaches the sink with no sanitization.]

security finding — Remote code execution via file upload; attacker can upload a file whose content is interpreted as a shell command [verified: Identical to finding 0: file-upload content flows unsanitized from UploadFile to do_os_system → os.system, attacker controls the executed shell command.]

OS Command Injection via File Upload (Quart) — Remote code execution via crafted file upload [verified: Same code path as idx 0 — uploaded file's first 20 bytes flow directly to os.system() at line 22 with no sanitization, middleware, or access control on the /files/upload route.]

Missing Authentication on FastAPI Trigger Routes — Unauthenticated attackers can execute command injection, code execution, deserialization attacks, and other dangerous operations through FastAPI endpoints. [verified: The FastAPI router in vulnerable.py registers all trigger endpoints via @router.get() with zero authentication dependencies, middleware, or guards. The app (apps/fastapi_app.py) includes this router unconditionally via app.include_router(vulnerable_routes) and adds no auth middleware—ContrastMiddleware is optional observability, not auth—leaving every RCE-capable sink (os.system, pickle.load, yaml]

Missing Authentication on All Sensitive Routes — Any unauthenticated attacker with network access can trigger dangerous operations including command execution, database modification, file reads, and deserialization attacks. [verified: No authentication mechanism (login_required, IsAuthenticated, middleware, or decorator) exists anywhere in the codebase—all command-injection, SQLi, deserialization, and code-execution endpoints are reachable by anonymous users across all 10 framework integrations.]

OS Command Injection via os.system — Remote code execution on the host server — attacker can run arbitrary shell commands [verified: Same data-flow as finding 0: user_input from HTTP request reaches os.system(command) at cmdi.py:5-6 through get_trigger('cmdi','os-system')(user_input) with zero sanitization — confirmed across all framework integrations.]

Insecure Deserialization via pickle.load() — Remote code execution — pickle payloads can execute arbitrary Python code and shell commands [verified: Same pickle.load sink on line 8-9 as finding 0; user_input from HTTP request is encoded to bytes and deserialized via BytesIO-wrapped pickle.load with no authentication or validation.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via urllib.request.urlopen — Outbound requests to attacker-controlled URLs enabling internal network scanning, cloud metadata access, and service pivoting [verified: do_legacy_urlopen passes user_input directly to urlopen() (aliased as legacy_urlopen); the @mock_connection gate is the sole control and is disabled by VULNPY_REAL_SSRF_REQUESTS=true in the Makefile, enabling full SSRF to arbitrary URLs.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via urllib.request.urlopen — Attacker can force the server to make HTTP requests to arbitrary internal and external hosts, enabling cloud metadata access, internal service scanning, and pivoting to internal networks. [verified: do_urlopen_str passes HTTP user_input directly to urlopen() with no validation; the @mock_connection gate is bypassed when VULNPY_REAL_SSRF_REQUESTS is set (Makefile exports it as true), enabling real outbound requests to any attacker-specified URL.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via HTTPConnection with user-controlled host — HTTP connections to attacker-controlled hosts enabling internal network pivoting [verified: Same as finding [1]—do_httpconnection_init passes user_input as the host to HTTPConnection() via _request_init; when VULNPY_REAL_SSRF_REQUESTS is set, real TCP connections to attacker-controlled hosts occur with no input validation or auth.]

Arbitrary Code Execution via exec() — Full remote code execution; attacker can execute any Python code including os.system calls, file operations, and network access. [verified: User input from HTTP query/header/form flows directly to exec(code) on line 2 with zero sanitization, validation, or auth — full arbitrary Python statement execution.]

Arbitrary Code Execution via exec() — Remote code execution with full Python runtime access [verified: Duplicate of finding [0]: exec(code) on line 2 with raw user_input, no controls — full remote code execution.]

security finding — Complete bypass of session authentication and CSRF protection; attacker can forge session cookies to impersonate any user [verified: Same underlying defect as findings #0 and #2: SECRET_KEY is hardcoded to 'test_key' in settings.configure() (line 27, not 24). The hardcoded secret is reachable on all three server paths with no external configuration escape hatch.]

Hardcoded Django SECRET_KEY — Attacker who knows the secret key can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, and signed data, leading to account takeover and privilege escalation. [verified: SECRET_KEY is unconditionally hardcoded to 'test_key' on line 27 of django_app.py inside settings.configure(), which runs on every app startup (runserver, uWSGI, and Gunicorn paths). No environment-variable override or external config exists. A known signing key allows forging Django session cookies and CSRF tokens.]

Reflected XSS via Jinja2 |safe Filter on User Input — Attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript via the user_input query parameter that is rendered unsafely in the Jinja2 template, enabling session hijacking and credential theft. [verified: User input from request.args.get('user_input') flows directly into a Jinja2 template rendered with the |safe filter (apps/templates/jinja/xss.html line 30), which explicitly disables auto-escaping; no CSP headers, sanitization, or middleware are applied.]

Reflected XSS in Bottle Route — Cross-site scripting in victim's browser [verified: Line 38 of src/vulnpy/bottle/vulnerable_routes.py concatenates request.GET/POST user_input directly into the HTML response string without any encoding or sanitization, and no CSP headers or middleware are set; Bottle returns string responses as text/html by default.]

XSS: " + user_input + "

" and returned as pyramid.response.Response without any HTML encoding, escaping, or CSP middleware — textbook reflected XSS with no compensating control.]

"`) at line 54 with zero encoding, sanitization, or CSP — no compensating control exists anywhere in the Quart blueprint or vulnpy codebase.]

security finding — Arbitrary file read through tarfile operations with user-controlled paths [verified: tarfile.TarFile.open(user_input) at line 7 accepts attacker-controlled path directly; no path traversal mitigation. Reachable via /vulnpy/pt/tarfile-open/.]

Regular Expression Denial of Service via re.search — An attacker can cause severe CPU exhaustion and denial of service by submitting crafted input that triggers exponential regex backtracking. [verified: do_re_search is auto-registered via TRIGGER_MAP as /vulnpy/redos/re-search/, receives raw user_input from _get_user_input(), and passes it directly to re.search(PATTERN, user_input) with the catastrophic-backtracking PATTERN=r'((a)+)+' — no timeout, validation, or rate-limit exists.]

Regular Expression Denial of Service via re.findall — CPU exhaustion and denial of service via crafted regex input. [verified: do_re_findall is auto-registered as /vulnpy/redos/re-findall/, receives unvalidated user_input, and feeds it to re.findall(PATTERN, user_input) with the same nested-quantifier PATTERN — no compensating control present.]

Regular Expression Denial of Service via re.sub — CPU exhaustion and denial of service via crafted regex input. [verified: do_re_sub is auto-registered as /vulnpy/redos/re-sub/, takes raw user_input and calls re.sub(PATTERN, 'anything', user_input) — the PATTERN triggers exponential backtracking with no timeout or input sanitization.]

Regular Expression Denial of Service via re.split — CPU exhaustion and denial of service via crafted regex input. [verified: do_re_split is auto-registered as /vulnpy/redos/re-split/, passes attacker-controlled user_input to re.split(PATTERN, user_input) — same catastrophic regex, same absence of any protective control on a reachable path.]

SQL Injection via str.format into cursor.execute — Arbitrary SQL execution on the SQLite database including data manipulation and schema modification [verified: Same do_sqlite3_execute chain; EXECUTE_QUERY_FMT.format(user_input) → cursor.execute at sqli.py lines 29-37, no parameterization.]

SSRF via HTTPConnection Constructor with User-Controlled Host — An attacker can force the server to make HTTP requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts, enabling port scanning, cloud metadata access, and pivoting to internal services. [verified: User-controlled input from the HTTP query parameter reaches the host argument of HTTPConnection() in _request_init with no sanitization. The @mock_connection decorator (ssrf.py:36) is a unit-test safety net, not a real control — the documented Makefile exports VULNPY_REAL_SSRF_REQUESTS=true, bypassing it entirely.]

security finding — XPath injection enabling unauthorized data access from XML documents and potential query logic manipulation [verified: Blanket finding confirmed: all three XPath trigger functions (lxml findall, lxml findtext, xml.etree findall) pass attacker-controlled user_input directly to XPath evaluators with no sanitization, escaping, or authorization.]

XXE via lxml.etree.fromstring — Local file disclosure, internal network SSRF, and denial of service via entity expansion from attacker-supplied XML. [verified: Attacker-controlled user_input from HTTP request flows unsanitized directly to lxml.etree.fromstring() at line 8 with no entity-disabling configuration; lxml resolves external entities by default, enabling file read and SSRF.]

Missing Authentication on WSGI Trigger Routes — Unauthenticated attackers can execute arbitrary shell commands, SQL queries, deserialization payloads, and path traversal through the WSGI application. [verified: The vulnerable_app WSGI handler processes all trigger routes including command injection, SQL injection, and deserialization without any authentication check, middleware, or decorator; the only middleware present is a path rerouter with no auth function.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting in WSGI Application — An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript into the victim's browser, enabling session theft, credential phishing, and arbitrary actions on behalf of the victim. [verified: Attacker-controlled user_input from query string (_get_user_input via parse_qs, line 24) is concatenated directly into HTML response at line 31 with no encoding or sanitization, creating a reflected XSS sink reachable via GET /vulnpy/xss/do_raw?user_input=<payload>.]

security finding — Exposure of sensitive configuration data, source code paths, SQL queries, and internal application state through verbose error pages [verified: Same underlying defect as findings #1 and #3: DEBUG=True is set in settings.configure() (line 28, not 25). The debug mode is unconditionally enabled on all reachable server paths with no compensating control.]

Django DEBUG Mode Enabled — Information disclosure via detailed Django error pages including stack traces, configuration values, and environment details that aid further attacks. This exposes stack traces, local variables, SQL queries, and the SECRET_KEY itself via verbose Django error pages to any caller.]

security finding — Denial of service: a single request blocks the entire event loop, preventing all other users from accessing the application for 10 seconds [verified: Same as finding 3: the async route's synchronous sleep(10) stalls the asyncio event loop with no rate limiting or thread-pool delegation, enabling trivial DoS.]

[verified: async /async_will_block route calls time.sleep(10) on the main event loop thread, blocking all other requests; no rate limiting, thread offloading, or any mitigation exists.]
